sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s from an accredited institution, completed by enrollment; no master’s necessary. Advanced calculus
and linear algebra competence expected. UChicago mathematics bachelor’s is an eligible credential route.
Department expressly considers international assistantship candidates. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Create/activate the application, select Mathematics doctorate, upload records and writing, enter three
recommenders, and indicate financial-assistance interest. Request any limited fee-waiver code before paying.
Resolve the official-score and statement discrepancies below before submission. [s1] [s2] [s3] [s7]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor agreement listed. Main requested-field fit is limited: current algebra faculty concentrate in
higher categories, homotopy and K-theory. Below are adjacent arithmetic/motivic contacts, not evidence of a
classical AG or number-theory group. [s1] [s8] [s9] [s11] [s13]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Student Status Page displays submitted documents and letters, allows additional uploads/contact updates, and
provides decision letter and accept/decline controls. [s3]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
Admission dates explicitly Fall 2027; several FAQ and aid paragraphs retain conflicting standing policies. [s1]
[s2] [s3] [s5]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [2027 confirmed]
PhD priority January 5, 2027; final May 10, 2027. Fall only; time zone unpublished. [s1]
Funding consideration [Conflict]
Current admission page gives January 5, 2027 PhD priority, while separate financial-aid page says all materials
by January 15 for assured aid consideration. Use the EARLIER January 5 date and ask whether January 15
remains valid. [s1] [s5]
Reference receipt; Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Complete file by January 5, 2027 priority; no explicit reference grace period. Central FAQ permits application
submission while letters arrive during review, but this does not guarantee late-letter consideration. Final official
records are due after acceptance; missing transcripts beyond first term block second-term registration under
central instructions. [s1] [s3] [s6]

Test-score receipt [Conflict]
Department requires official language scores by application review and FAQ calls files incomplete without
officials. Central instructions instead accept uploaded unofficial English/GRE reports for review, with officials
only after admission. Obtain written clarification; send officials in time for January 5 if testing is necessary. [s1]
[s2] [s3]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
Central Graduate Studies FAQ states funded fall offers cannot require commitment before April 15; exact offer
acceptance deadline is in the offer and may differ for unfunded admission. Confirm current Fall 2027 terms. [s6]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
TOEFL minimum 90 before January 21, 2026 or 5.0 thereafter; IELTS 7.0; PTE 61. Valid two years; no Duolingo,
IELTS Indicator/One Skill Retake, TOEFL MyBest or Essentials. TOEFL Home Edition accepted. Institution code
1105. [s2] [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
Completed bachelor’s or higher from an institution primarily teaching in English qualifies; indicate education
waiver in application. Completed UChicago degree qualifies. Current wording does not expressly include an
unfinished degree at application, so confirm if applying before conferral. [s1] [s2] [s3]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional but preferred; if supplied, considered in admission. No minimum. Institution code 1105. [s1] [s2] [s4]
GRE Mathematics [Conflict]
Conflicting official wording: current Mathematics PhD overview calls both General and Math GRE optional but
preferred; department FAQ answers no to recommending Math Subject and says it is not required. Math GRE is
clearly not mandatory; degree of preference needs clarification. [s2] [s4]

sections.text:
Transcripts and degree records [Conflict]
Upload unofficial transcripts from every postsecondary institution; English certified translations as needed.
Final official degree-conferred transcript is necessary after acceptance. Department FAQ suggests officials
before admission, while central instructions request them after acceptance and place a second-term hold if
missing; confirm actual timing. [s2] [s3]

whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three academic letters, preferably recent instructors able to assess mathematical preparation; an employer
letter may suit applicants long out of school. [s1] [s2]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
No separate assistantship form. Indicate financial assistance in the main application. No extra scholarship
statement/reference is identified on mathematics aid page; award-specific requirements remain unverified. [s5]
[s7]

What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
Department FAQ says choosing online recommendation and supplying referee email sends a request. Central
guide describes an emailed link for rating plus letter, but exact save/button timing is not explicit. [s2] [s3]
Before versus after submission [Conflict]
You may submit before letters arrive; central FAQ says they are linked as they arrive during review. Interfolio
accepted: central FAQ says list each referee and mark mailed recommendation; instruction page says enter
Interfolio contact and have committee file emailed to program. Confirm which portal method to use. [s3] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
Student Status Page displays submitted documents and letters, allows additional uploads/contact updates, and
provides decision letter and accept/decline controls. [s3]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Additional documents can be uploaded, but replacement of a completed confidential reference and cross-cycle
reuse are not specified. Files not enrolled for more than two years require reapplication and resubmission of
documentation. [s3]

sections.title: Written materials
sections.text:
Academic CV / resume [Standing rule]
Required uploaded CV/résumé; length and formatting not published. [s3] [s4]
Statement of purpose; Research-interest statement [Standing rule]
Central required SOP is 1-2 pages. Prompt paraphrase: reasons for graduate study/program choice,
personal/professional goals, prior research and research interests. Upload; public font/spacing/file-type rules
absent. Department permits emailing a PDF to mams-staff@case.edu if unable to insert it or already submitted.
[s2] [s3]
Personal / background statement [Conflict]
Program overview says both SOP and personal statement, while department checklist lists personal statement
and central instructions specify SOP. It is unclear whether these are two documents or different labels for one.
Exact separate personal prompt/length is unverified; confirm before drafting. [s1] [s3] [s4]
Research proposal; Publications list; Course-list document [Standing rule]
Not listed as a separate required item on the public mathematics application checklist. This does not establish
whether the current portal permits an optional upload; exact prompt, length, formatting and upload/link rule
are not published. [s1]
Writing sample / thesis / research summary [Standing rule]
Central instructions say writing samples should ONLY be uploaded for a named list of other programs;
mathematics is not on that list. Do not add a math paper/thesis as a writing sample without permission. [s3]
Scholarship essays [Standing rule]
No separate assistantship form. Indicate financial assistance in the main application. No extra scholarship
statement/reference is identified on mathematics aid page; award-specific requirements remain unverified. [s5]
[s7]
Other short answers / materials [Standing rule]
If applicable, PhD research questions request up to four significant experiences with institution, average
weekly hours and months. Conduct yes-responses require circumstances, dates, institution/court and outcome;
these answers are not shared with department or used in application review per central page. Exact field limits
unverified. [s3]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Standing rule]
Selected PhD assistantships include tuition and a living stipend; mathematics publishes no numeric stipend. Do
not borrow stipend figures from English or biomedical programs. Exact paid months, fees, insurance and
summer coverage require the offer. [s5]
Years of support; Conditions and duties [Unresolved]
No published fixed guarantee length. TA recipients teach or assist instruction; support is available only to
selected PhD students, not every admitted student. [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department FAQ explicitly asks about international assistantship access and affirms equal opportunity; no
blanket international exclusion is published. [s2]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
No separate assistantship form. Indicate financial assistance in the main application. No extra scholarship
statement/reference is identified on mathematics aid page; award-specific requirements remain unverified. [s5]
[s7]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Department offers teaching and research assistantships; central Graduate Studies directs applicants to their
program for institutional awards. Other fellowship citizenship criteria are not established. [s5] [s7]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 85 nonrefundable, credit card only. Complete application requires payment or valid waiver. [s2] [s3]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Limited first-come departmental waiver codes; criteria vary by year. Central instructions direct severe-hardship
applicants to their program. Ask mams-staff@case.edu before payment; waiver is not guaranteed and no
public separate deadline is provided. [s2] [s3]
